sources.summary: CDC's 32-slide investor day deck, released by Infratil on 16 September 2026. Slide 9 ('Construction is progressing to meet FY27-29 deliveries') says CDC 'is well underway at all sites where customer capacity has been contracted, with all data centres under construction to be delivered across FY27-29'. Under 'Sydney Marsden Park' it reports 'Substantial investment underway to deliver multiple large scale data centres at CDC's Marsden Park campus across FY28-29'. Slide 6's campus map (status legend as at 30 June 2026) shows Sydney Marsden Park MP1 as an operational data centre, MP2 to MP5 as data centres under construction and MP6 as future development. Slide 8 lists 'Sydney Marsden Park 1' among seven data centres delivered since FY25. The FY28-29 delivery timing is a forecast.

sources.title: City of New Albany, Ohio: data-center information site home page (version modified 26 October 2026)
sources.summary: The City of New Albany's data-center site home page says that New Albany has been home to data centers since 2010 and that 15 companies operate 40+ facilities. Its 'Neighbor Noise Update' says: 'The City of New Albany is working to address noise complaints from neighbors near two active data center sites, one operated by Google and one operated by Meta.' Under 'Google' it says residents near 'Google's New Albany campus' reported cooling-fan noise in September 2025 and that Google has implemented mitigation including sound monitoring, operational adjustments and sound-dampening materials, with a permanent solution scheduled for completion in December 2026. Under 'Meta' it says that in July 2026 the City was notified about periodic noise from 'Meta's New Albany data center campus south of SR-161', reported after a temporary sound wall was removed 'as construction neared completion', and that Meta's steps include 'changes to current operations' and 'Installing a temporary sound wall along Morse Road while construction continues'. Compared with the previous (26 August 2026) version, this version replaces the 'Resident Questions' card and menu item with a new 'Utility and Behind-the-Meter Power FAQs' card and menu link; the noise-update text is unchanged.

sources.title: Minnesota Public Utilities Commission: Notice of Public Hearings and Availability of Draft Permit, North Rochester to Skyway High Voltage Transmission Line Project (PUC docket E002/TL-26-135), issued 31 August 2026
sources.summary: The Commission's notice, issued 31 August 2026 in the matter of the application of Xcel Energy and Echo Zone LLC for a route permit in Goodhue County (PUC docket E002/TL-26-135; Court of Administrative Hearings docket 24-2500-42002), says the applicants, Northern States Power Company (Xcel Energy) and Echo Zone LLC, a subsidiary of Google LLC, propose an approximately 1.2-mile double-circuit 345 kV line connecting Xcel Energy's North Rochester Substation to four new substation facilities at the proposed Pine Island Industrial Planned Unit Development site, with an 11.3-acre expansion of the North Rochester Substation; the line and expansion will be owned and operated by Xcel Energy and 'the four Project Skyway substations will be owned and operated by Google'. Construction is proposed from May 2027 with an in-service date of December 2029. It sets public hearings on 14 and 15 September 2026 and comments to 25 September and 9 October 2026, states that the Commission issued a draft route permit on 14 August 2026 that does not authorise construction, and notes Xcel's 14 April 2026 petition for approval of an electric service agreement with Echo Zone, LLC, a subsidiary of Google LLC (docket E002/M-26-170). Its project overview map (page 6) shows the proposed substations inside the 'AUAR Development Area' east of US 52. The notice establishes that Google's Project Skyway at the Pine Island Industrial PUD site is a pending, identified project; it is not a consent for the data-centre development.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is the notice's stated issue date, 31 August 2026 (PDF created 26 August 2026; posted on the PUC project page on 4 September 2026 and published in the EQB Monitor of 8 September 2026, us-midwest-iowa-ne-p5-eqb-monitor-v50n36-20260908). The copy was obtained from the Environmental Quality Board's public document service (EQB record 269414, document handle 4871810) because the PUC eDockets host answered robots.txt with HTTP 403. The draft-permit date, hearing dates and construction schedule are recorded as stated; scheduled work is not a stage.
sources.personal_data_note: The notice names Commission, utility and company contacts with e-mail addresses and telephone numbers and an administrative law judge; none are copied.

sources.title: ATC news release: 'ATC files revised application for the Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project' (posted 15 September 2026)
sources.summary: ATC, the transmission owner, says it has filed a revised application with the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin (PSCW) for approval of the Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project, which it says is 'needed to support increased electric load in the Port Washington area'. The release states that 'The customer at the Lighthouse campus is committed to paying its own way when it comes to the energy needed to power its facilities' and to fully funding the cost of the transmission infrastructure built to serve it. ATC first applied in September 2025; after the PSCW revoked the completeness determination for that application, ATC prepared the revised application, which designates the South East route as preferred in the southern portion, removes the east-west route through the towns of Trenton and Saukville, adds an E-STATCOM next to the proposed Decker Substation and includes up to five new substations with new and rebuilt power lines across Calumet, Fond du Lac, Manitowoc, Sheboygan, Ozaukee and Washington counties. After the PSCW finds the application complete it will announce public-comment opportunities; the project also needs Wisconsin DNR review. The grid works are proposed and unapproved.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is 15 September 2026, the 'Posted on' date printed on the release (ATC's post sitemap, atc-post-sitemap-20261027.xml, gives lastmod 2026-09-14T16:41:57-05:00 for the same URL, i.e. the post was prepared the day before its stated posting). It dates ATC's announcement of the revised filing. Power-readiness context only: it is not a data-centre status observation and does not change the campus's 19 October 2026 construction observation.

sources.title: ATC project page: Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project (PSCW docket 137-CE-229), captured 27 October 2026
sources.summary: Project status: 'Filed a revised application with the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin in September 2026.' Project need: 'The proposed project will support growing electric demand in the region, including the Port Washington data center project'. The PSCW docket is 137-CE-229. The southern portion would build two new dual-circuit 345-kV power lines connecting the proposed Decker Substation in Port Washington to the existing system and rebuild lines between the proposed Mullet River Junction (Sheboygan County) and Cedar Creek Junction (Washington County) substations; the northern portion would build a 345-kV connection from Forest Junction (Calumet County) to the proposed Sheboygan River Substation (Fond du Lac County); the Decker, Sheboygan River, Mullet River Junction and Cedar Creek Junction substations (and Adell, if the South East route is chosen) would be built. Milestones: approval 'TBD'; construction anticipated 31 days after the PSCW's written order; in service about 17 months after construction begins (forecasts). Contact names and telephone numbers on the page are not copied.
sources.date_semantics: The page carries no publication date; ATC's project sitemap (atc-project-sitemap-20261027.xml) gives lastmod 2026-09-17T14:59:57-05:00, consistent with the September 2026 revised filing it describes. Context for the project's identity link to the Port Washington data center and for the docket number; no observation date is taken from it.

sources.title: Oracle blog: 'A Responsible Path Forward for Project Lighthouse' (16 September 2026)
sources.summary: Oracle, the campus customer, says it is 'partnering closely with American Transmission Co. on its revised certificate of public convenience and necessity application for the Ozaukee County Distribution Interconnection Project', that it is 'committed to paying 100 percent of our energy costs' under the PSCW's VLC (very large customer) tariff approval order, and that 'More than 50 percent of the power capacity to serve the campus will come from carbon-free energy such as wind, solar, and batteries', with the rest matched by renewable purchases. It repeats Project Lighthouse's expected economic impact and job figures and says 'Our commitment to completing Project Lighthouse remains unchanged.' No capacity, energisation date or construction stage is given.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is 16 September 2026, the date in the blog's byline and URL. Power-readiness context: it ties ATC's revised interconnection application to the Project Lighthouse campus from the customer's side. Not a status observation.

sources.title: Alliant Energy: 'Data centers' page (our-energy/data-centers), captured 27 October 2026 (sitemap lastmod 26 October 2026)
sources.summary: Under 'Data centers within Alliant Energy's service area' the utility lists 'Meta | Beaver Dam, Wisconsin': 'Meta announced its $1 billion data center investment in Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, in November 2025. The project will be built in Alliant Energy's Beaver Dam Commerce Park.' It adds that 'Meta will also underwrite nearly $200 million in energy network improvements, substations and transmission lines to support the project', that Meta will donate $15 million to Alliant Energy's Hometown Care Energy Fund over the next decade, and that 'The site's electricity use will be matched with 100% clean and renewable energy.' The page also describes Alliant's data-centre rate safeguards and lists QTS and Google in Cedar Rapids and a potential QTS campus in Clinton, Iowa. No capacity, energisation date, substation name or construction stage is given.
sources.date_semantics: The page has no printed date; Alliant's sitemap (alliant-sitemap-20261027.xml, captured 27 October 2026) gives lastmod 2026-10-26 for it, so the captured text is the utility's current statement as of 26-27 October 2026. Power-readiness context only; it is not a status observation and the Meta record's 9 October 2026 observation is unchanged.

sources.title: Alliant Energy news release: 'Meta announces $1 billion Data Center Investment in Beaver Dam, Wisconsin' (12 November 2025)
sources.summary: The utility's release of the joint announcement says the AI-optimised campus of more than 700,000 square feet 'will be located in Alliant Energy's Beaver Dam Commerce Park', described as Wisconsin's largest certified site, shovel-ready since its WEDC designation in 2019, and that 'As part of its commitment to cover infrastructure costs to support the data center, Meta will underwrite nearly $200 million in energy infrastructure investments including network upgrades, utility substations, and transmission lines.' It gives Meta's expectation that the data center will come online in 2027 (a forecast) and names Alliant Energy as the utility serving Beaver Dam.
sources.date_semantics: published_at is 12 November 2025, the dateline of the release (sitemap lastmod 2025-11-12). Original statement of the grid commitment repeated on the current data-centers page; context only, outside any status window and not used as an observation. The 2027 online date is a forecast.
